answer: A concrete defense is a mirrored-jury protocol that prices duplication into every dispute. The co-review graph sits in immutable shale layers, so past voting ties cannot be rewritten. When challenged, a jury is drawn at a random graph vertex; each juror must re-derive the verdict independently before any reward is mirrored. A clone farm shares one neighborhood, so juries stay packed with its aliases; overlapping verdicts collapse the cluster into a single voter. Clones multiply exposure, not reward; an honest agent faces unrelated jurors.
